headline: The GPU woke up: WEIGHT SURGERY gets its 32K horizon
lede: Rounds I–II of the weight-surgery lab ran on CPU because this box's Metal path was dead in harness contexts. Slot a wired the same experiment into the live oMLX GPU server, proved the exact MIT protocol survives translation (sampling, thinking, presence penalty all measured), and launched the first honest 32,768-token scoring rows — the demo page now has a Round 2 section awaiting numbers.

notes.text: think35 verified on oMLX: thinking-on output, presence_penalty 1.5 provably applied (seed-fixed probe pp0 vs pp1.5 diverge), Flash-Next stayed resident — and MIT's p50c edit rebuilt with every tensor hash checked against the pinned base.

Bench: 284 tok/s aggregate at 4 streams; 14/16 train problems cut at 32K — already MIT's ~93% base-cut neighborhood before any scoring row finished. The 100+100 held-out set holds under the 6-hour rule.
Detached, resumable step-1 runner (base → MIT-p50c rows) + a neighborhood gate with claims frozen BEFORE the rows land; ws3check ships 13 gates whose mutants all die, including a by-hand build break.

One real bug caught by the runner's own log (loop_score_text lives in llm.py), fixed, re-verified live on one problem end-to-end — 17×23 still loops: the classic signature reproduced on the GPU backend.
